owns: Whether an explicitly identified external-reference claim — general, domain, or institution-published knowledge that is not a household fact — is recorded with the provenance and freshness a reader needs before relying on it, and which Atlas explanation surface it may inform.
does_not_own: Household facts, balances, rates, limits, dates or terms of any household account; Forecast inputs or outputs; owner policy; transaction or provider evidence; financial permission; or any independently sufficient authority for a household financial calculation or action. Forecast remains the sole household calculator. A record here may inform explanation only; it owns no financial value.
coverage: Explicitly identified knowledge IDs recorded as items below. CI proves record shape, provenance, freshness, informs pointers, and the closed exclusion list. It does not verify a claim against the institution and does not claim semantic completeness over arbitrary Markdown.

external-reference.meaning: A claim about the world outside the household — an institution's published process, a market convention, a rule of thumb — recorded with its sources and the date it was checked. It is not household data and never carries the verified / calculated / estimated / unknown household trust tags.
external-reference.may: Inform explanation of an already-published Atlas or Forecast result.

items.subject: TD closed-mortgage early-renewal window, rate hold, and renewal contact timing
claims: TD lets a closed mortgage renew early up to 120 days before maturity with no prepayment charge and no fee.
TD's standard rate hold is 120 days, extendable to about 150 days for existing clients. A held rate is a floor, not a commitment.
TD normally makes renewal contact four to five months before maturity and posts the offer letter about a month before maturity. The posted renewal rate is an opening offer, not a fixed price.
A mortgage left unsigned at maturity typically rolls to a short open or posted-rate term, which costs materially more.
Switching lenders needs approval, appraisal and discharge, so the 120-day window is also the point at which a switch becomes practical.

provenance.method: Public web pages read during the 2026-08-09 Atlas research session. No institution login, no household account data, no provider feed.

freshness.review_reason: An institution's published renewal process and its existing-client extension can change without notice. Re-read the TD source before the household acts on any date derived from this record, and at least every 90 days. After review_by, treat the claim as needing re-checking, not as current.
